data.narrative:
QuEra Computing is a Series B quantum computing company founded by a team including Mikhail Lukin and Vladan Vuletić, competing in a sector represented by 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, and PsiQuantum. The company has raised $230M to date.

Valuation was triangulated using stage-progression analysis, the only applicable method given data constraints. A $6M proxy based on total raised was stepped forward using a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $11.4M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable: while 8 quantum computing competitors exist in the broader dataset, the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier peer groups produced insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to support a reliable median. Applying a sector-wide median would introduce unacceptable selection bias given stage and capital-intensity variance within quantum computing.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $13M, with $11M as the central point. This range reflects the mechanics of stage-based progression applied to the company's raised capital. Material uncertainties include the absence of comparable Series B quantum computing transactions, heterogeneous technology approaches across the peer set, and nascent commercialization timelines across the sector. A widened search for transaction data or milestone-based anchors would strengthen confidence in this estimate.
